q: Which set of seven labels is entirely correct for a drawing of a chloroplast?
options: Outer membrane, cristae, matrix, thylakoid, granum, glycogen granule, 80S ribosomes
Outer membrane, inner membrane, stroma, thylakoid, granum, starch grain, 70S ribosomes
Double membrane, stroma, nucleolus, granum, thylakoid, 80S ribosomes, central vacuole
Inner membrane, intermembrane space, cristae, lumen, matrix, starch grain, circular DNA
explanation: Chloroplast labels: outer and inner membrane (the envelope), stroma (fluid containing Calvin cycle enzymes), thylakoids (flattened membrane sacs), grana (stacks of thylakoids), stroma/intergranal lamellae, thylakoid lumen, starch grains, lipid droplets, 70S ribosomes and naked circular DNA. Cristae and matrix are mitochondrial; nucleolus and vacuole are parts of the cell; plants store starch, not glycogen.
